name: Essential amino acid supplements
short: A review warns most amino acid supplements may not be risk-free and can cause detrimental side effects; an 8-week knee osteoarthritis trial found no protein allergy or significant lab differences.
text: Direct safety evidence for essential amino acid mixtures is limited in the cited sources to one randomised trial: in 65 people with knee osteoarthritis given leucine-enriched essential amino acids or control for 8 weeks, there were no related generalised or local protein allergic reactions, and blood counts, serum glucose and kidney and liver measures did not differ significantly between groups. A review of the side effects of individual amino acid supplements (not essential amino acid mixtures as such) concluded that enhanced intake of most amino acid supplements may not be risk-free and can cause detrimental side effects, and called for research into their suitability in the elderly, in children, in pregnancy and breastfeeding, and in people with diabetes or liver disease; the abstract does not say which harms apply to which amino acid. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
